speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the cause of Singtel's broadband Internet service disruption on 3 December 2016; and (b) what can the Ministry do to strengthen and protect critical infrastructure, such as the telecommunication network, from major disruptions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of the resiliency of Singapore's broadband networks given the service disruptions by our Internet service providers (ISPs) in recent months; (b) how does the network availability of Singapore's ISPs compare internationally; and (c) whether there are measures that the Ministry is planning to improve the resiliency of our networks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over the past three months, both Singtel and StarHub have suffered service disruptions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Infocommunications Media Development Authority (IMDA) is investigating the Singtel disruption on 3 December 2016 and will provide more details soon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The DHCP server assigns IP addresses to end-users' modems, so that the end-user can connect to the Internet.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Unfortunately, SingNet's DHCP server encountered problems assigning IP addresses to its broadband customers' modems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As a result, these customers could not obtain or renew their IP addresses in order to connect to the Internet.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA and the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) are also investigating the October 2016 incidents affecting StarHub subscribers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More details will be shared in the Prime Minister's response to another question later.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: My Ministry and IMDA take a serious view of all service difficulty incidents, as they inconvenience consumers and businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We continuously review measures to enhance the resilience of Singapore's key telecommunication networks and services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, IMDA regularly reviews and updates the Telecom Service Resiliency Code.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Code was most recently revised three months ago to strengthen the resilience of our fixed and mobile broadband networks, given how pervasive they are today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA had also issued a Code of Practice for Telecommunication Infrastructure Resilience Audit − also known as the Mobile Audit Framework − in 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This Code of Practice requires mobile operators to conduct regular audits on key aspects of their networks and infrastructure, such as network designs, technical processes, business continuity plans and associated infrastructure and facilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA has conducted an audit on the mobile operators' networks and has found that they are generally compliant with the audit controls.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will continue to finetune the audit controls to cater for technology developments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While direct comparisons are not possible due to differences in methodologies and network designs, our studies show that our networks are generally as resilient as our international counterparts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, few jurisdictions besides Singapore actively track ISPs' network availability and, those that do, typically set a threshold lower than ours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will continue to update the QoS framework to ensure that operators continue to provide good quality of service to consumers and business users.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Instead, we expect operators to plan and design resilient networks, and put in place measures to ensure speedy recovery in the event of a disruption.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will minimise inconvenience to end-users should such disruptions occur.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will he also assure us that this disruption was not due to any form of cyber attacks and that the Ministry is fully capable of dealing with any form of cyberattacks?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As to whether or not we have the ability to deal with cyberattacks in future, we will have to continue to build up our defences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is something which CSA is committed to and we will work with all the sector leads to ensure that they have put in place programmes, and more importantly, mitigation efforts to deal with any disruption that occur.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister mentioned about our benchmark are not available against international operators, but within Singapore's context where we are moving towards a smart nation and more connected services, are we still expecting 99.9% as the benchmark or could we be more resilient than that?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Certainly, what is also important is the amount of time it takes to get services back to normal.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does the Ministry plan to enhance standards in that respect?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On that earlier clarification on cybersecurity, if I recall the StarHub incident, there were also DDoS attacks where they took over certain devices on the network.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am quite surprised that this could happen on our public networks.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What measures could be put in place to ensure that security is not compromised in the future?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Certainly, we will continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Attacks, as the Member rightly pointed out, can come from the most innocent of devices, in this case, the Internet of Things devices that happened in America.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, it is something in which we are mindful where we need everyone within the value chain − the businesses and even consumers like ourselves − to put in place some cyber hygiene practices at home and in our workplaces.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will work closely with the industry and industry associations to ensure that all our businesses understand what needs to be done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will work with the major operators who provide the service to the small companies so that they understand what needs to be done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As the CSA Chief Executive Mr David Koh mentioned, cybersecurity is a team sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have to continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is very difficult for us to determine ahead what exactly they need to do because the networks are becoming very complex and technology is developing very rapidly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: That is something we will continue to do.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Minister mentioned my question about 99.9% being too high and should be lower.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is actually the opposite; I meant it is too low.
